A document may now leave out the llm block. A restricted table (the ICPSR studies, NCVS 38604, the a2aj case law) refused with 403 says to accept the terms at https://data.rmorie.com/terms.

  • API calls no longer end a reply that is slow to start: a model that thinks before answering is not cut off by the 30-second low-speed limit.

  • It shows that it is working. While a model thinks, the terminal shows a turning spinner, “ is thinking” and the seconds so far, then how many help pages it has read; the line is wiped when the answer comes. Only for a person at a terminal (never in a script, a log or options(morie.quiet = TRUE)); Ctrl-C now ends a long wait for a model.

  • A repeated question is answered at once. The answer to the same question (spacing aside; case counts), on the same route, model, packages and versions, is kept on this machine for 30 days and comes back without asking the model: rmbl ask says so, --fresh (R: fresh = TRUE) asks again. Owner-only files under tools::R_user_dir(), at most 200, outdated ones removed on each save, the first save in a session says where; only for a person at a terminal (the command line with the terminal on stdin and stdout) or an interactive session, never from a script, a pipeline or a check; MORIE_LLM_CACHE=off turns it off. Nothing is hosted.

  • Servers can reuse the instructions. The instructions a model gets are the same for every question (the functions picked for a question travel with the question), so the prompt caches of Ollama, OpenAI, DeepSeek and Gemini apply, and long instructions are marked for Anthropic’s cache: a faster, cheaper first answer on every route.

  • Better retrieval. The help search matches inflected words (“emissions” finds “emission”, “testing” finds “test”) and leaves out question words; the closest help pages go with every question, to large models too; and the model is told never to say the packages lack something before it has searched under other words.

  • bricklayer_explain_error() and rmbl explain-error "MESSAGE": where an error or warning of rmoriebricklayer, rmoriedata or rmorie comes from, without a model or the network. Every message is read from the packages’ own code (stop(), warning(), usage errors; sprintf() and paste() parts as wildcards), matched exactly or by its words, and traced to the exported functions that reach it, whose help pages say what they expect. With no argument, the last error of the session. rmorie’s 18,000 messages are read once per installed version and kept beside the saved answers.

  • Ollama has to be running. rmbl doctor and the help now say to start it (ollama serve, the Ollama app, or its system service) when nothing answers at its address. ## Network and statistics stress tests of 5e1dce5 (2026-10-14)

  • A typo, a file name or a key is never sent to a model. A line with no verb is asked only when it plainly is a question: the first argument is the question itself (two words or more, or ending in ?), it is not a verb or one or two letters from one, it holds no path, line break or key-shaped word, and anything after it is an option ask takes (rmbl "how?" --fresh works). rmbl explain-eror "object 'x' not found", rmbl "My Documents/urls.txt" and rmbl conifg set anthropic.key "$(cat key.txt)" with a CRLF key file went to the model before, the key with them. An unknown verb now names the nearest one (did you mean ...); one that looks like a key is not printed back.

  • A Ctrl-C during a GET is raised (rmbl models exited 0 with “did not answer”, a Wayback run polled on past its time limit): the transfer’s callback records the interrupt it takes. The plain GET behind the Wayback lookups takes Ctrl-C too.

  • The key prompt finds stty and sh on PATH without a child process (only /bin and /usr/bin were looked in, so on a NixOS-style layout the key was echoed), runs the sh it found, and takes a Ctrl-C already pending before the read starts. config setup prints its key explanation as part of the prompt the shell shows once echo is off.

  • A settings or cache folder left open by an earlier version is made owner-only, not only a new one. config set writes only the settings it changes into llm.json (a full rewrite cut floats to 4 digits, unboxed arrays, renamed a "" key and rounded integers past 2^53). Answers are kept only with a person at a terminal or in a GUI session (R --interactive < file kept them). The note after the tool-call cap goes with the last tool result (Anthropic and Gemini got two user turns in a row).

  • The native CSV reader: a table that would decompress past 512 MiB is read the streamed way (read.csv(gzfile()); a 2.6 MB file of blank lines got the process killed for memory), and a .csv.gz that is plain text is read as such. As read.csv() reads them: unquoted header names are trimmed (" Operational_Capacity " came out X.Operational_Capacity.), CR and CRLF inside quotes are newlines, a line holding only "" is blank, blanks before a quote and text after one are kept. A quote inside an unquoted field (ab"c, where read.csv() swallows the rest of the file) is refused in words. Deliberate differences from read.csv(): a UTF-8 byte-order mark is not part of the first name, and extra fields and an unclosed quote are refused. Short rows are filled, as read.csv() fills them, unless filling makes more cells than the text has bytes plus ten million (a 2,000-column header over short lines made 4e8 cells from a few megabytes). A Ctrl-C while a table is inflated or split is looked for every million fields or blank lines (by rows it waited 53 s on a wide table), the inflating goes in 16 MiB steps on its second pass too, and either comes back as R’s interrupt, not an ordinary error.

  • Survey replicates: what is refused, what is said and what cannot be told apart is in ?survey_design. New: a copy of the weight within 1 percent on every row is refused under JK1, JKn and BRR; warnings for more replicates equal to the weight than a bootstrap draws (judged against the m!/m^m chance for the PSUs read from the replicates), a near copy under the bootstrap or Fay, a JK or BRR replicate that leaves no row out and is no rescaled weight, and replicates totalling on average under a tenth or over ten times the weight ($repweights multipliers), and a replicate over ten times the weight on a typical row (api99 among the bootstrap replicates raised the SE 21% in silence). 360 generated genuine sets: 0 refused, 0 warned; survey’s JK1 and bootstrap subsets of apiclus1: no warning. A second column with the id’s name and other values is refused (it was kept); the weight beside the replicates under its own name is recognised within 1e-12.

  • Reordered survey data is caught by a key per row, computed every time: rows reordered within strata or PSUs are refused now, a permuted outcome (a permutation test) is not a reorder, and a million rows of ten columns take 0.6 s per estimate (the per-column digests took 88 s). Only the columns the design uses must have unique names.

  • hurwitz_zeta() with a whole q beside the trivial zeros goes through Riemann’s zeta and the finite sum (5.4e-8 relative at q = 2 near s = -30); 144 points against mpmath at the exact doubles agree to 3e-15.

  • knox_test() compares incidents too far out for the distance band to index with every other one directly (one outlier at 1e300, or a band of 1e-300, refused the whole test), and measures distances in band units. hotspot_persistence(): a period whose hot set a tie emptied has no overlap to report (it showed 0); the courts vignette says how ties work.

  • Refusals in words: a NULL, empty or missing column name in plr_crossfit(), exposure_response_plr(), exposure_concentration_index() and pollution_burden_by_area(). missingness_summary() and duplicate_rows() take data with duplicate column names, which is the messy data they exist to inspect.

  • Tests: none reaches a real host without RMBL_LIVE_TESTS=1 (online_now(), the LinkingTo fallback, an invalid.invalid lookup, a route test’s status lookup); the tibble reorder test resets row names as a tibble does (it passed on builds that never compared values).

CI on 84840ac, and asking in other words (2026-10-14)

  • aye, tellme, or just the question. rmbl aye "...", rmbl tellme "..." and rmbl "how do I weight a survey?" all ask, with every option ask takes. A first word that is no verb is asked when a word holds a space or the last word ends in ?. A lone unknown word is still an unknown verb, so a typo is never sent to a model.
  • Ctrl-C reaching the top level exits 130. The launchers (inst/bin/rmbl, inst/bin/rmoriebricklayer, and what install_cli() writes) catch an interrupt that gets past the command’s own handler, which exited 1 with “Execution halted” on the release legs of 84840ac. A Ctrl-C in the first tenth of a second, while R itself starts and before the package loads, is R’s own and still exits 1.
  • A Ctrl-C just before a key prompt is no longer lost. The prompt looked for sh and stty with Sys.which(), which runs a child process. R ignores Ctrl-C while a child runs, so the interrupt killed only the child. The prompt then fell back to a read that ignores Ctrl-C, and the command waited. They are now found on disk, with no child process.
  • The otis-mrp bundle runs again. analysis.R sources the package’s argument checks (aaa_input_guards.R, lib_helpers.R) before the package files it loads on its own. Those files call .rmbl_arg() since the match.arg sweep, and the bundle check failed with “could not find function”.
  • Keys from earlier logins. A key a pre-0.5.12 login saved for https://llm.rmorie.com (the retired gateway, the same issuer and key store) goes to the signed document’s data address again, instead of asking to sign in anew. Any other address stays bound to itself.
  • A spent time budget stops the help lookups. When no time was left for another turn, the error was taken for a model that cannot use tools, and the question went out again without them, with a full timeout. It now stops with the time-budget message.
  • Schema check warning. The misspelling check on structural invariants compared names of two lengths and warned “longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length”.
  • Coverage. The coverage job runs the live transport checks, as the check job does.
  • This package names no package built on it. bricklayer_llm_ask() and bricklayer_explain_error() read this package’s help and messages by default; before, they also loaded rmoriedata and rmorie when those were installed. A package built on this one passes its own (packages =), and its command line sets RMBL_PACKAGES (comma-separated) for the verbs it hands over, as RMBL_PROG names the command.
  • explain-error announces a long read by its size. The “Reading the messages …” note came only when rmorie was among the packages; it now comes for any set of namespaces over 5,000 objects (rmorie has 18,709, this package about 1,200).
  • No warnings in the build or the tests. The checked writer’s message buffer holds a whole path (gcc -Wformat-truncation); two unused Keccak helpers and an unused constant are gone (clang -Wunused). The tests expect the warnings they provoke: the stability bound, the exhausted XMSS key and the record switched off.

Re-test of 46de6a9 (2026-10-14)

  • Survey replicates: an explicit contract, nothing guessed. The totals and constancy checks added in 46de6a9 refused 13.5% of 1,320 genuine sets (a dominant PSU; a jackknife replicate constant on a subset) while a data column still rode along with replicates taken from the analysis file. Every value heuristic is gone. The replicates are exactly the columns you give, by name or as the object passed: a column of data passed under its own name is a replicate because it was asked for. What is refused is exact: the full-sample weight itself (for a jackknife, BRR or Fay design; a bootstrap replicate that draws every PSU once is the weight, legitimately), the id’s values, the row numbers, a column of data passed under another name, and a name collision with the weight or the id whose values differ. A genuine replicate that shares the id’s name is kept. A reordered tibble with a vector weight is caught: the design keeps a digest of every column as given and sorted, and the same values in another order are a reorder whatever the row names say; a column changed afterwards is not.
  • The prompt goes once. A model call is never retried: a POST that timed out may have been read by the provider. A conversation with help-page lookups that runs out of its time budget says so instead of shrinking the last call to five seconds; past the cap of 12 tool calls in a turn the rest are dropped from the turn and the model told, rather than 3,000 “not run” rows being sent back. rmbl models and any GET take Ctrl-C; so does a gzip decompression.
  • The answer cache makes a stored answer printable on the way out (an answer cached by an earlier build carried a clipboard write), writes through a fresh temporary name, treats a file that is not a record as a miss, and takes MORIE_LLM_CACHE as off, 0, false, no, none or disabled (spaces aside), and the option as those words too. A script run at a terminal with stdin and stdout on it is a person watching; </dev/null, a pipe or a redirect is not. Model names from a server and config values print clean. The saved settings directory is created 0700 whatever the umask.
  • Wayback. The daily-limit default message is what wayback_retry() looks for, so a URL captured already today is left for tomorrow; the per-run resubmission cap counts only resubmissions since the last capture that got through, so a slow archive finishes.
  • Tests run in a fresh, empty config directory with the developer’s saved keys, hosted key and MORIE_DATA_URL unset; every test that reaches the live internet needs RMBL_LIVE_TESTS=1.
  • Pre-0.5.12 logins stored the address of the retired model tier; such a key is withheld with a message, so those users log in once more.
  • The curated tables load in a fraction of the time. A gzip-compressed CSV is decompressed by the checked reader, split into columns in C and typed as read.csv() types it (plain integers, decimals and TRUE/FALSE/T/F decided from the bytes, everything else by type.convert()): the same table, byte for byte of meaning, in a fifth of the time (a million-row table: 1.3 s where read.csv() took 6.6 s). A record with more fields than the header and a quote that never closes are refused in words.
  • Hot spots made by a tie are not hot spots. When the cells tied with the k-th busiest would make more than twice k cells hot, the tied group is left out (tied_out says how many, and printing says so); cell = 0.1 on even counts no longer calls 100 of 100 cells hot.
  • Refusals in words, every time. A choice argument given a wrong value says what it must be and what it got (match.arg()’s “‘arg’ should be one of” named neither); a data frame with an empty or repeated column name is refused before anything is looked up; drift_psi(bins = ) takes one whole number up to a million; clearance_decomposition(base = ) takes one of the two values of compare and keeps its type; an estimate without a standard error plots without a warning.
  • hurwitz_zeta() beside the trivial zeros takes the distance to the nearest integer exactly before sinpi() (R’s sinpi(x) beside x = -1 is sin(pi * x), which loses the digits of a value of order that distance: up to 8.9% at -2 +/- 1e-15, on glibc as on other libms); the test compares against mpmath at the exact doubles. A whole q of 2 or more beside the trivial zeros goes through Riemann’s zeta and the finite sum (5.4e-8 relative at q = 2 near s = -30 before). crime_density() keeps every incident on a map that runs past 180 degrees (the points are in the grid’s frame). hotspot_persistence() says when it drops an incident without a location or period. A planar cell index past 2^53 is refused rather than merged with its neighbours. A burden at rate 0 or population 0 draws. The age-specific rate message in pollution_burden() and its siblings no longer says such a rate cannot exist.

Review of 29a55d8 (the stress round of 2026-10-14)

  • Ctrl-C while a model thinks is a Ctrl-C (G1). The wait consumed the interrupt and the POST came back as a dropped connection, which was retried: the prompt went to the provider twice and the answer printed. The interrupted POST now raises the interrupt (exit 130 from rmbl ask, one request at the provider), and nothing is retried after one.
  • A stored key stays bound to its address (G2, G3). With the model tier off the comparison had no address to compare against, so a key saved for another server went to the data service, and a new login recorded no address. The address is now the data service’s when the document names no model tier; login --token checks the key at the signed document’s address only, never at MORIE_DATA_URL.
  • The answer cache is for a person at a terminal (G4). It wrote from rmbl ask in a script or a pipeline (the command line always turns the progress option on); now it needs the terminal on stdin and stdout, or an interactive session. The question keeps its case (df$X is not df$x), the stored question is checked on a hit, and the first save in a session says where the answers go.
  • Wayback status-reply throttles stop (G5). A throttle in the status reply requeued the URL and the next job id reset the strike count: one URL made 174 POSTs. Strikes now reset only when a capture gets through, the eighth stops the run, a run resubmits at most as many times as it has URLs, the target page’s own 503 and bandwidth errors fail that URL rather than count as account throttles, and a job id that reads like an error code is refused.
  • The XMSS lock is released whatever happens (G6). The lock is taken and the locked call run in one C frame whose cleanup is the release (R_ExecWithCleanup): an on.exit() handler is R code an interrupt can cut short before its .Call, and 73 to 95 locks per 5,000 interrupts stayed held; 5,000 interrupts now leave none. A record whose name starts with another’s keeps its temporary files.
  • Survey replicates (F1, F2, E9 residual). Replicate columns taken out of the analysis file itself (replicates = d[paste0("bw", 1:24)]) are accepted again; a genuine replicate under the weight’s name is refused, not dropped; a replicate that sums to less than a fifth or more than five times the full weights (a row number, an id, survey’s multiplier matrix) or is the same for every row (a constant) is refused. survey_compare(ref = 2023) takes the number as the label.
  • crime_density() near the antimeridian (F4) draws: grid nodes past 180 degrees keep their continued values when wrapping would put them out of order. hurwitz_zeta() past the double range is a signed infinity, not NaN. (This entry first called F5 a reference artefact; it was a real loss of digits, fixed in the re-test above.) knox_test() drops an incident without a location or time and says so, as its siblings do; hotspot_persistence() says when it drops (0, 0); max_pairs = TRUE is refused; the planar cell key writes whole numbers in full.
  • Model and provider text is made printable (L1): answers, model lists, the spinner’s model name and error bodies lose screen-clearing, title and clipboard escapes. Tool calls keep the text-only contract (L2): a nameless call is answered in words, the dataset filter is plain text, at most 12 calls are run per turn, an empty reply is “returned no text”, never "". A key with a line break is refused (L3) in R and in C, so it never becomes a second request header. The settings file is written through a fresh temporary name (L5). A conversation with help-page lookups gets three times one call’s timeout (L6). The progress frame takes a NaN time. An assumption with ok = NA prints as NA. The age-specific rate message no longer says such a rate cannot exist. The live transport tests need RMBL_LIVE_TESTS=1 exactly, and the model tests clear a developer’s own endpoint and keys (L4).

Review of e57fed5 (the stress round of 2026-10-13)

  • The spinner frame stays in its table (E1). rmbl_progress_spinner(), a public C-callable, cast t * 10 to an integer, which overflowed past about 9e17 (nanoseconds) and read another table’s string; the frame is now taken in double, so every time maps to a frame. A bar wider than an int is clamped before the cast (E13).
  • The gzip reader’s memory is bounded by its output (E8). It inflates twice: once into a 64 kB scratch buffer to check everything and count the output (a bomb is refused having held 64 kB), then straight into the result, allocated once at its size; one zlib state serves every member, and more than 100,000 members are refused. A million empty members (20 MB) had taken 3.56 GB, a 4 MB bomb 3.19 GB; both are now refused within a few megabytes. Each kind of damage is named (a bad CRC, a length trailer that does not match, a damaged header, no gzip magic), not all as a CRC failure. A 600 MB file under a 3.5 GB memory limit is read; under a smaller one the report says the memory ran out, as an error report.
  • Bulk archiving keeps to archive.org’s limits (E7). Captures start no faster than per_minute (default 6; the SPN2 documentation allows an account 7). A slow-down reply, as a 429 or inside an HTTP 200 (error:user-session-limit and the other throttle codes the SPN2 documentation lists), holds every submission back for its Retry-After or 15 s doubling to 10 minutes, and sends the URL again; eight in a row stop the run. The account’s daily cap stops submitting. Status checks that fail back off the same way. max_captures (default 1000) caps a run; the rest are left for the next. Before, 300 URLs went out in 32 s.
  • No test captures a page on archive.org (E6). The live test runs only with RMBL_LIVE_TESTS=1, and never posts to /save.
  • Wayback reply handling. A job id that is not a short token (TRUE looped for ever, 123 stopped the run) is a failure; two URLs given one id each keep their entry; a timestamp that is not one is recorded as missing, and a results file holding one reads back; a reply over 64 kB is not parsed. An API call takes its answer only from the host it asked: after a redirect to another host, that host’s JSON had been recorded as archive.org’s; the transport now refuses such a redirect for API calls (Save Page Now, model endpoints, OCSP), and reports Retry-After. An http page is looked up (it is a parameter of the lookup, never fetched); a key file other users can read is warned about; a URL with a control or bidirectional character is refused, and printed results show only what the URLs show. A run that is stopped records the captures it had started, and the next run polls them instead of sending them again; a missing folder for the results file is refused before anything is sent. wayback_retry() looks failures up one a second and leaves a daily limit hit today for tomorrow.
  • Survey replicate columns are only replicates (E9). A column holding the full-sample weight, the id or any other column of data is refused by name (the full weight given as a vector and the id had been averaged in: a standard error of 0.2599 or 0.2704 where it is 0.2836), BRR and Fay replicates must come in a Hadamard order, and a matrix with a class of its own is read as the matrix. The full weight named in weights and shipped beside the replicates is dropped by name, as before.
  • Wilson at 0% and 100% (E2). The interval is Wilson’s at the respondents (the design effect is 0/0 there): 40 of 40 gives [0.912, 1], where it collapsed to [1, 1]. The logit interval takes the same at the ends. The degrees-of-freedom factor of the modified effective sample size is (t_(n-1) / t_df)^2, as the SAS documentation gives it (it was (z / t_df)^2; the same for a large n).
  • Survey design. New type = "jkn" with rscales (JKn weights passed as JK1 overstated the standard error by 37%); the replicate design’s degrees of freedom are the rank of the replicate weight matrix less one, as the survey package computes them (twelve BRR half-samples of an eight-stratum design have 8, not 11), or degf. survey_estimate() checks the data is the design’s rows in the design’s order (reordered data gave a wrong answer silently). A design with no stratum of two PSUs has no variance to report: the standard error is missing and flagged, not zero; a certainty stratum is not a lonely PSU; the flag for a domain whose weights are all zero says so. by = character(0), conf_level = NA and a two-element ref are refused in words.
  • (0, 0) is “no location” in Knox too (E3). knox_test() drops it, as crime_density() and hotspot_persistence() do (twenty such rows had made the closest cell 163 observed against 33 expected). The three share one way onto the plane: points across the antimeridian are one place, and an extent past 2,000 km is said. crime_density() refuses a bandwidth longer than half the earth’s circumference and says when one is ten times the incidents’ spread; knox_test() checks max_pairs; hot spots made by ties are counted (tied_in) and said when they are most of the active cells.
  • One rate band for every pollution entry point (E4). pollution_burden(), pollution_burden_by_area() and mortality_displaced() take a rate per person-year between 1e-5 and 0.1 (1 to 10,000 per 100,000), rare_outcome = TRUE below and high_rate = TRUE above, as verify_pollution() now does on its rate per 100,000 (0.5 had been taken as a rate per person-year: 14,634 deaths from a million people). verify_pollution() passes the switches on to its stages. pollution_report_text() refuses a list that only looks like a report.
  • The bundled TPS data, one row per occurrence (E5). Rebuilt from the Service’s Break and Enter file by data-raw/tps_break_enter_d14_2024.R: 508 occurrences (the Service publishes one row per offence record; five occurrences have two, kept as offence_records), every one located. The old file’s all-NA row was a subsetting artefact (an NA year in a logical index), and it carried one 2025 occurrence and missed one of 2024. The vignette’s Knox ratio is computed from the data. The lone 2026 court row is gone. Sources and licences: inst/COPYRIGHTS, and the DESCRIPTION’s Copyright field.
  • The manifest (E10). An empty dataset list does not replace a cached manifest that lists tables, and a table the manifest does not list is not loaded unverified.
  • The XMSS record (E11, E12). Temporary files carry their record’s name, and a writer removes only its own record’s (with three records in one folder, 117 of 900 writes had failed); the lock is taken with interrupts held off and released by a handler registered before it. A record of 100,000 keys is read without the regular-expression passes: a whole signature took 0.5 s on an x86-64 laptop (the documentation said 0.7 s; the reviewer measured 1.4-1.8 s).
  • The 02a38be leftovers. hurwitz_zeta() uses the functional equation for Riemann’s zeta at negative s (full relative accuracy beside the trivial zeros) and no longer overflows a Bernoulli polynomial whose value is finite (hurwitz_zeta(-4, 5e61)). The terminal prompt is printed by the shell that reads it, once its trap is set and the echo is off, and a read that never finished is an interrupt (a Ctrl-C in the first milliseconds had exited 2; a key typed at once was echoed). bricklayer_llm_status() and rmbl models say a key is stored for another address instead of “not logged in”. An empty schema is said to check nothing (and refused by apply_schema_validation()); only a one-letter slip or a swap in a structural invariant’s name is taken for a misspelling (min_data_cols is a field of its own). Printing keeps the zero-width joiner and non-joiner, variation selectors and flag tag sequences. drift_calibrate(n = 0) is refused. The README counts the 8 entry points written in plain C. The exposure CSV reader no longer runs two regular expressions over the whole text to see whether it is blank.

Retrying a bulk Wayback run

  • New: wayback_retry() and rmbl wayback --retry FILE.jsonl. Reads the results file of an earlier wayback_save() run and retries every URL whose latest result is a failure: each is first looked up in the Wayback Machine and recorded as existing when a capture is already there (the daily limit’s refusals, pages captured by another run), the rest are captured again into the same file, and pages their source no longer has (HTTP 404 or 410) are left alone unless include_gone = TRUE (--include-gone). Returns the whole run as it now stands, with the retry’s counts.

Timing tests

  • dudect: both classes are written the same way. The 150-tick ML-KEM compare-and-select was flagged intermittently on GitHub’s x86 runners (|t| up to 30). Its compiled code is branch-free with a fixed memory access pattern; the difference came from the harness, which copied the fixed class into place and generated the random class in place, leaving the slots in different cache states. Random inputs now go through the same copy, and a new target, mlkem768_fo_select_validity, compares a pool ciphertext against itself and against another, both made by the same code, so only the match bit differs. Every target shows no evidence of leakage locally (x86-64, max |t| 2.8) and the positive control is still flagged.

Hot spots over time, and rates over time

  • New: hotspot_persistence(). Incidents counted in grid cells per period: the share of places holding half the incidents (the law of crime concentration), the hot cells (the busiest top share, ties included) and their share of incidents, the Jaccard overlap of each period’s hot spots with the previous period’s, and per cell how many periods it was hot. Plot: the concentration and persistence over time and a map of the cells by how often they were hot.
  • plot() of a rate takes period =. A rate by group and period draws one panel per group, the rate as a line over its interval band on a shared scale.

Complex survey estimation

  • New: survey_design(), survey_estimate(), survey_compare(). Design-based means, totals, proportions and ratios, overall and by domain, with variances from replicate weights (Statistics Canada’s bootstrap, mean bootstrap, jackknife, BRR, Fay’s BRR) or from Taylor linearization over strata and PSUs with a finite population correction and a choice for single-PSU strata. Domain estimates keep the whole design. Replicate totals are computed in C straight from the data frame’s columns (CSUS 2023: 36,180 respondents by 1,000 mean bootstrap weights in about 1.6 s). Proportions default to the modified Wilson interval of SAS PROC SURVEYFREQ that Health Canada’s published CSUS intervals use. Estimates, standard errors and intervals match the survey package to machine precision for linearized, JK1, bootstrap and Fay designs, domain estimates and contrasts; CSUS 2023 lifetime cannabis use reproduces Health Infobase’s published percentages from the public-use file. Domains under 30 respondents are flagged (Health Canada’s suppression rule), not withheld. Plots for both.

A new look for every plot

  • One theme across all 33 plot methods. The plot region is a tinted panel crossed by white major and minor grid lines (bricklayer_plot_options(panel = ), NA for none), with no box and softer axes. Intervals are translucent bands with haloed points; lines carry a soft fill to the axis and a labelled, emphasised last value; bars sit on the panel with a sheen along the leading edge and their value at the end; the sequential palette runs deeper for fields and heatmaps. Drift calibration draws each column’s false-alarm rate with its exact interval over the splits (an all-zero result drew an empty frame). Axis titles, row notes and panel keys shrink and wrap to fit; labels that fit are not cut.
  • Every plot is in the examples. ?plot-methods draws every class, the courts and crime plots on the shipped data included, and vignette("plotting-results") gains a courts and crime section.

Small bases compute

  • yoy() and rate_change() report every percent change. A small base no longer withholds the percent: 2 to 20 reports +900% with its exact rate-ratio interval, and a change of a few tenths of a percent off a base of 15 is reported as such. min_base now defaults to 0 for every unit and, when set, only adds a “small base” note; min_count likewise notes without hiding. Only a zero base has no percent change. Printed, CSV, Markdown and HTML footers say “note” where they said “percent withheld”, and the period-over-period plot draws small-base percentages.
  • compute_footprint() no longer reads 0 g for fast work. A call shorter than the elapsed clock’s resolution had 0 s of wall time and so 0 energy; the duration is now at least the CPU time spread over the cores. plot() of a footprint shows CPU, memory and total in one unit chosen to fit (kg to micrograms), and says “Too short to measure” when even CPU time is 0.

Archiving in bulk, and animated progress

  • New: wayback_save() and rmbl wayback FILE. Save many URLs in the Wayback Machine with archive.org’s Save Page Now 2 API and your account’s S3-like keys (IA_S3_ACCESS_KEY and IA_S3_SECRET_KEY, or ..._FILE naming files that hold them). Several captures run in flight at once through the package’s own checked libcurl transport; a page captured recently is kept (within), a page captured already today is recorded with that capture, rate limits and server errors back off and retry, a refused key stops the run, and each result is written to a JSON Lines file as it lands so an interrupted run carries on where it stopped. Run live with real keys on the ledger’s sources before release.
  • Animated progress, drawn in C. src/rmbl_progress.c renders the bar (a shimmer along the filled part, a head that fills in eighths and pulses while work goes on, a spinner) in 24-bit colour or plain, block characters or ASCII; the R side eases it to each new value at up to 12 frames a second, only on a terminal a person is watching, with milestone lines elsewhere and NO_COLOR honoured. bricklayer_download() and wayback_save() use it, and rmbl_progress_bar() / rmbl_progress_spinner() are C callables for the MORIE packages that link to this one.

Courts and police-reported crime

  • New: case_flow(), life_table(), disposition_mix(), clearance_decomposition(), crime_density() and knox_test(), each with print and plot methods. The clearance rate with exact intervals and months to clear the inventory; the actuarial life table for banded times (equal to Kaplan-Meier at the band edges without censoring, checked against survival::survfit()); outcome shares with Goodman’s simultaneous intervals and Cochran-Armitage trends; Kitagawa’s decomposition of a change in a clearance rate into rate and case-mix effects with a Mantel-Haenszel rate ratio and a Simpson’s-paradox verdict (on the Court’s own figures, 2014 to 2022: the aggregate fell while the rate at a fixed mix rose); binned Gaussian kernel density with highest-density regions (checked against MASS::kde2d()); and the Knox test with exact expected counts (checked against a full enumeration of permutations).
  • Real data in inst/extdata (?justice-data): Ontario Court of Justice monthly flow and time to disposition (2024-2026), outcomes, offence groups and courts by calendar year 2012-2025, each reconciled to the published provincial totals; Toronto Police Service break and enter occurrences in division D14, 2024. Vignette courts-and-crime.
  • Plots fit the device. Multi-panel plots choose rows and columns from the device (one row squeezed four panels into a 3.5-inch device); y-axis titles sit outside the tick labels actually drawn (a five-digit tick label overprinted the title at line 3) or are left off when there is no room; the key under lettered panels is measured at the size it is drawn (strwidth() scales by par("cex"), which a panel grid lowers, and mtext() does not, so the key ran off the device); the plume and particle titles fit their panel.
  • apply_schema_validation() checks for a data frame before the schema.

Review of 02a38be (the sixth pass)

  • hurwitz_zeta() is accurate below s = 1. The Euler-Maclaurin shift added in the fifth pass summed |s| + 20 terms and cancelled them against a small result: every digit was lost below s = -5 (zeta(-11) came back as 5.4, zeta(-15) as -2.3e7, where 52a8883 had returned NA), and near s = -5 only six digits were right. Now s <= -5 uses Hurwitz’s Fourier formula on (0, 1] (exact zeros at the even negative integers, zeta(-200, 2) = -1 exactly), -5 < s < 1 Hermite’s integral on [1, 2), the integer s in (-5, 0] the Bernoulli polynomial, and any other q is shifted into range by sums that do not cancel. Checked against mpmath at 40-60 digits over 112 points: the largest relative error is 1.9e-13. A tiny q keeps its own term (hurwitz_zeta(0.5, 1e-20) was Inf). The fifth pass’s test compared against a reference that was wrong in the fifth digit with an absolute tolerance that accepted 0; it is relative now.
  • A truncated or damaged compressed exposure file is refused. R’s gzfile() returns what a cut gzip or bzip2 file decodes to, with no error and no warning, so half a file was read as a whole one (status ok). gzip is now inflated in C with zlib, every member’s CRC-32 and length checked (several members, as gzip -c a b and data.table::fwrite() write, are read whole); a bzip2 file must end with its end-of-stream marker; an xz decoder warning is an error. The decompressed size is capped while it is read (options(rmoriebricklayer.maxcsvbytes), 1 GiB): a few megabytes of gzip no longer grow to gigabytes before anything is refused. zlib is now a system requirement (it ships with R’s own build dependencies).
  • A baseline rate below one per 100,000 needs rare_outcome = TRUE, whatever its unit. The check ran only when baseline_rate_per was missing, so a wrapper or do.call() that always passes it turned 0.008 per person-year into 0.008 per 100,000 and a burden 100,000 times too small, with status ok. The check is on the converted rate now, and below 1e-6 per 100,000 no rate is accepted (baseline_rate_per = 1e300 was).
  • A NAPS value column with "<2" is refused, as an exposure column is. The value was converted before the text check and counted as a row with no measurement (prevalence 1.0 instead of 0.4).
  • --force belongs to config reset alone. config set own.key --force stored “–force” as the key. config show, help, get and unset refuse extra arguments, and arguments after a bare -- are refused by every verb but ask and bundle (functions -- a b listed everything).
  • A FIFO, device or directory at the legacy record path is refused at once. The migration read it with file.exists() only, so a FIFO blocked signing for good while the lock was held.
  • Parallel manifest refreshes no longer collide: each writes its own temporary file (one shared name let them delete each other’s, 11 of 12 workers failed). A reply that is not a manifest ({}, an error object, a datasets that is not a list of tables) is refused and the cached copy kept.
  • A cached table is deleted only when it fails a known digest. Offline, a stale manifest that lists the table without a digest now loads it, as the live manifest does; with no manifest at all the cached table is refused but kept for the next run, where it is checked again before use (it was deleted, and had to be downloaded again).
  • Ctrl-C at a prompt exits 130 where /bin/sh is dash (Debian, Ubuntu). The shell’s trap ran, but system2() reported no exit status for it, so the interrupt came back as an empty line and a usage error (exit 2, or 1 at the e-mail code prompt). The trap now also prints a marker R recognises. The fifth pass’s test mocked system2(); this one runs the launcher in a real terminal (util-linux script), under dash and bash.
  • The CSV reader: a UTF-32 file with a byte-order mark is read (its decoding error quoted a kilobyte of the file); a row with more or fewer fields than the header is refused by line number (it wrapped into an extra row); a column name given twice is refused (the second column was ignored); a numeric exposure column is no longer turned back into text to be searched (15 of the 24 s on a 102 MB file).
  • A next_index past 2^31 - 1 is the damaged-key error, not a raw NA comparison error.
  • apply_schema_validation() needs something to validate against: NULL, an empty list or a provenance without schema (a typo such as scheme) is an error, not TRUE. A schema field a few letters from a known one (expected_colums, min_data_row) is fatal with a “did you mean”; other unknown fields are said. expected_dtypes, the name the provenance files use, is checked as expected_types (the OTIS file’s column types never were), and a factor matches a character column.
  • A hosted key saved for another address is said once per session, and ask with no route says the key is stored for the other address instead of “no key stored”.
  • data list removes every default-ignorable code point (soft hyphen, U+034F, Hangul fillers, U+180E, the byte-order mark, the interlinear annotation marks, tag characters), not only the bidirectional and zero-width ones.
  • The credentials file is read as bytes: a NUL byte, a file that is not UTF-8 and a file over 1 MB are refused with a plain reason (a NUL silently cut the file, a 10 MB file took minutes).
  • A temporary record file left by a writer that died mid-write is removed at the next write.
  • verify_pollution() refuses a non-numeric scalar such as as.raw(25); the dispersion solvers refuse n_steps past 2^31 - 1 even with max_work = Inf, and a particle grid larger than max_work cells; plot() of what is not a pollution report says so.
  • Plots fit small devices: the margins are scaled to the figure at the text size in use and the labels are cut by their measured width (cex = 2 on a 2-3 inch device failed, and a 4-inch plot cut labels it had room for); the bar for missing values never takes a real level’s name.
  • The record documentation gives the measured cost: about 0.7 s per signature at 100,000 keys.
  • The lock wait is interruptible (one non-blocking attempt at a time, the wait in R); releasing descriptor 0, 1 or 2 is refused; the record writer checks the written size and flushes the directory after the rename (the fifth pass’s NEWS said “size-checked” before it was); a lock file owned by another user is named as such, not as a read-only directory. The barrier generator registers the five entry points written in plain C directly (they throw no C++ exception) instead of stopping, and the README counts both kinds.
  • Tests: a test compared a mean with its own formula and now checks two independent predictions.

Review of 52a8883 (the fifth pass over the branch)

  • A tampered cached table no longer loads when the manifest cannot be fetched at all. The fourth pass covered only the retry: when the cached manifest was over a day old (or absent) and the server was down, the first manifest read failed, that failure counted as “no digest”, and the tampered file loaded and stayed. Now a manifest that cannot be had is never “no digest”: the check falls back on the last manifest on disk, however old, and with no copy at all the table cannot be verified and is not kept. A refreshed manifest is written beside the cached one and moved over it only once it parses, so a failed refresh no longer destroys the copy the fallback needs. The fourth pass’s NEWS item below overstated what it covered.
  • The XMSS used-index record is locked by the operating system. The lock directory of the fourth pass was taken over after 60 s by check-then-delete, which let two signers hold it at once and sign one index (reproduced 1 time in 60), and spun for ever on a lock it could not delete. The record is now locked with flock() (Unix) or LockFileEx() (Windows) on xmss_used_indices.txt.flock, in C: the kernel releases the lock when the process ends, so a crashed session leaves nothing to take over, and the 10 s wait is bounded and draws no random numbers (lock contention no longer moves set.seed() streams). A read-only directory is said as such.
  • The record is written in C and checked. It is written to a temporary file, flushed to the disk with fsync(), size-checked and only then renamed over the old one; a full disk stops the signature and leaves the old record in place (it emptied the record before).
  • A key’s record id is a fingerprint of its secret seed, not the root field it carries: a stale copy whose root was upper-cased, padded or swapped is still the same key, and a signature whose root does not match the seeds is withheld (its index stays retired).
  • A key built from given seeds is not registered at birth: it may have signed elsewhere, so it signs from index 0 only after xmss_register_key() vouches for it.
  • The record of the releases before 0.5.12 is migrated: xmss_index.json next to the record is read and merged, and kept as xmss_index.json.migrated once the new record is written; an unreadable one stops signing. Lines of the 0.5.12 pre-release format are read as well.
  • The record path must be an absolute path to a regular file (or to one that does not exist yet): /dev/null, a directory, "none", "-" and relative paths are refused.
  • xmss_advance() without message accepts a signature index only up to the highest index the record shows this key has used here, so an edited index cannot burn the leaves in between; a bundle is accepted as documented; a damaged next_index is a clear error. xmss_forget_used_indices(key) takes the signing key (the record is keyed by its seed). The help says what to do in CI or a container with a fresh home directory.
  • verify_pollution() reads gzip, bzip2 and xz CSVs again (the byte reader of the fourth pass refused them as “NUL bytes”), decodes UTF-16 without a byte-order mark, and stops on a parse problem such as an unbalanced quote instead of returning the rows before it (status ok with mean 12.2 instead of 36). The decoded text is parsed from a file, not a text connection, so a large file is no longer several times slower, and it is held once rather than with a file-sized logical vector beside it.
  • A baseline rate below one per 100,000 is accepted when its unit is given (baseline_rate_per = 1e5 for a rare outcome, 1 for a rate per person-year); the note now says which to pass. Exposure cells that are text rather than numbers ("<2") stop the run and are named, since dropping them biased the mean and the prevalence; empty and missing cells are dropped and the report prints how many. exposure_csv with demo = TRUE, a population above ten billion and an empty income column are handled with a reason.
  • credentials.json is validated with the real parser before it is edited, and the edited text is parsed again before it is written: bare words, missing or trailing commas, trailing garbage and duplicate keys are refused instead of written into (every later read failed).
  • rmbl config setup reads the MORIE key and your own API key without echo, and the echo is switched off and on by the shell child itself, so Ctrl-C cannot leave the terminal silent; Ctrl-C at any prompt exits 130. A key given on the command line (login --token KEY) is warned about. data list, data pull, functions, config path and config setup refuse extra arguments. config reset moves a readable file only with --force, never overwrites an earlier backup, and is listed in the help.
  • hurwitz_zeta() sums a negative q in closed form: no cap, no billion-term sum, and none of the cancellation that returned 0 for s = 5 at q = -99999.5; below s = 1 it returns the analytic continuation (hurwitz_zeta(0.5, 0.5) is -0.6049).
  • lagrangian_particles() has the max_work cap of advection_diffusion_2d() (particles x steps); gaussian_plume() and gaussian_puff() take at most 1,000 lid image pairs; a step count above 2^31 no longer fails in the report title.
  • Bar labels cut to fit stay distinct (a number tells apart levels the cut made identical), a real level named (missing) keeps its name, and labels are cut to the device’s width.
  • print() of an attestation or bundle written by 0.5.9 to 7703a04 warns that it carries the signer’s private key. fips_verify_mu() returns FALSE for an edited verifier key instead of an error, and a scheme given as two names is refused. hill_tail_index(x_min = factor(...)), cramers_v(bias_correct = "abc"), cramers_v(min_expected = NA), plot_funnel() with a bad levels or target and pollution_report_text() of a non-report are refused with a reason.

Review of fcdce03 (the fourth pass over the branch)

  • A tampered cached table loaded when the manifest could not be re-read. The digest retry of the second pass re-fetched the manifest on a mismatch and, when that fetch failed, had no digest left to compare and accepted the file. The digest the check started with now stands unless a refreshed manifest is actually fetched and lists another; a failed refresh refuses the file. A manifest digest that is a list, or not a digest, refuses the file and removes it from the cache; a MORIE_DATA_URL that is not the document’s address is named in the error.
  • The XMSS used-index record is locked and fails closed. Every reservation runs under an exclusive lock directory next to the record, so two processes signing with copies of one key cannot both take an index (and two keys cannot wipe each other’s lines); the record is one line per key (xmss_used_indices.txt), written through a unique temporary name whose rename is checked; a malformed line stops signing until the file is repaired or removed; the off switch warns on every signature; a value that is not a path (TRUE, "0") is refused. pqc_keygen() registers every key in the record at birth, so a key the record does not know that claims never to have signed is refused (a deleted record, or a key from another machine) until xmss_register_key() vouches for it or xmss_advance() carries it forward. xmss_advance() checks the index against the key’s height, verifies the signature when the message is given, never advances below what the record knows, accepts an attestation, bundle or recode manifest, and warns when the key is exhausted; xmss_forget_used_indices() can forget one key and is documented as removing the protection. Examples and vignettes point the record at a temporary file so checks and builds leave the configuration directory alone.
  • verify_pollution() reads the exposure CSV whole: UTF-16 is decoded, a UTF-8 BOM dropped, a file that is not UTF-8 read as Latin-1 and said, NUL bytes refused (the fifth pass found a quote that swallowed the rest of the file still did, and that compressed files were refused). population = NULL or baseline_rate = NULL is an error report with a reason. baseline_rate may be zero (a measured zero); a value between 0 and 1 per 100,000 fails the assumption and suggests baseline_rate_per = 1, the new argument for a rate quoted per person-year.
  • hurwitz_zeta() refuses q below -1e6 instead of allocating the recurrence’s billion terms; logical q, x_min, fractions and non-logical discrete/approx are refused.
  • advection_diffusion_2d() has one cap for every run, max_work (100 million cell updates, Inf lifts it): the same physics costs the same whether the caller sub-steps it or the scheme does, so a run cannot be refused in one spelling and accepted in another.
  • credentials.json is edited as text: login and logout touch only this package’s three members and every other byte (another package’s floats, large integers, empty keys, non-ASCII text) stays as it was.
  • The review’s section-1 leftovers: print() and capsule_bundle_read() warn about an old object that carries key_state; an edited verifier key object is “not verified”, not an error; verify_pollution() refuses scalars beside a CSV or the demo, refuses list and complex scalars, says how many non-numeric exposure rows it dropped and skips the equity index when fewer than two rows have an income; bar labels over 28 characters are cut so a long level cannot make the figure margins too large; own-endpoint settings without an address are said when the hosted tier is used instead; OLLAMA_BASE_URL in the environment wins over a saved address; own.key and own.url in one call keep the key; rmbl config reset moves an unreadable settings file aside and doctor reports the file instead of failing; verbs that take no arguments refuse extra ones and Ctrl-C exits 130; U+061C, U+2028 and U+2029 are stripped from listings; a schema that is not a list is a clear error; a stack within half a kelvin of the air has zero rise (no cliff); Anguilla uses Antigua’s grid and Jersey and Guernsey France’s; Ukraine’s 2022 row is named as such; a note line is never under a tenth of an inch and one inline note no longer shrinks every page of a yoy_pdf().
  • Tests: a tampered cache with a failed refresh, two processes signing with one key, a malformed and a deleted record, the off switch, Latin-1 and UTF-16 CSVs, the large negative q, the cap’s consistency, and the credentials bytes.

Review of 7703a04 (the second pass over the branch)

  • The XMSS signature object carried the private key too. The attestation fix of the first pass stripped key_state from attestations only; capsule_sign() itself still returned the advanced key, with sk_seed and sk_prf, inside every XMSS signature, so every shared signature, bundle JSON file, chain and report made with XMSS from 0.5.9 to 7703a04 handed out the private key, and anyone holding one could attest or sign anything under the victim’s root. The signature object now carries no key material of any scheme, and the next key state is xmss_advance(key, signature) (new, exported, with xmss_forget_used_indices()). Treat every XMSS key whose signature, attestation, bundle or report left your machine under 0.5.9 to 7703a04 as compromised: generate a new key and sign again. A test checks that no signature, attestation, bundle, JSON or serialisation of any scheme contains private-key bytes.
  • XMSS index reuse across sessions: the registry of used indices now persists in xmss_index.json under tools::R_user_dir("rmoriebricklayer", "config") (the directory CRAN policy sets aside for a package’s own configuration), so a key reloaded from disk with a stale next_index is refused on the same machine, in a fresh session too. The option rmoriebricklayer.xmssidxfile or RMBL_XMSS_INDEX_FILE moves the file; "" or FALSE turns it off. The record does not travel with the key: save the advanced key after every signature, as before.
  • verify_pollution() with a mean but no prevalence (or the reverse) is an error report (exit 2), not “ok, 0 cases”: the first pass’s zero-exposure fix had made the omitted input a silent zero. Both scalar defaults are now NULL. A per-100,000 baseline_rate below 0.01 fails an assumption as a per-person rate typed in the wrong box; an exposure above 10,000 ug/m3 fails the range assumption instead of throwing; a UTF-8 BOM, a negative row and a date are handled; the attributable-fraction step is inside the report contract.
  • The French SIU resolver keeps a line break that ends a stripped boilerplate sentence (the first pass replaced it with a space and glued the next roster line, or the next section header, onto it); the property test now inserts the sentence at the line end too.
  • advection_diffusion_2d() caps only runs that sub-stepping inflates: a large stable run is the caller’s to wait for. The number in the message is formatted properly and the advice is correct (a smaller dt lowers the sub-step count). lagrangian_particles() refuses more than 100 million particles; gaussian_puff() warns about receptors below ground or above the lid.
  • plot() of a frequency table with a missing level draws it as “(missing)” instead of failing on the margin (broken since 0.5.11).
  • HMAC capsule_verify() answers FALSE to any edited signature field; capsule_check_attestation() accepts a public-key object as key_expected (for XMSS the root and seed both) and reports a missing digest instead of throwing.
  • Language models: a local Ollama selected by model or key at the default address that does not answer is announced before the hosted tier is used; a setting of the wrong type in llm.json (route: 5, an array, true, "") is an error, not “auto”; a credentials file without hosted_base_url (morie writes one) sends the key only to the services document’s address; MORIE_DATA_URL receives the stored key only when it is the document’s curated-data address; login and logout keep another package’s entries byte for byte (the file is edited as text); a saved address may not contain whitespace, a fragment or user information.
  • rmbl data list strips the C1 controls and the bidirectional format characters as bytes, in any locale; the help never shows --token KEY.
  • bricklayer_data_load() refuses a manifest digest that is not a digest (a sha256: prefix is accepted), and a mismatch refreshes the manifest once before calling the file bad, so a table rebuilt upstream does not fail until the cached manifest expires.
  • apply_schema_validation() warns when the provenance list has no schema (a typo such as scheme is no longer silent) and refuses an environment.
  • Territory proxies: Saint-Barthélemy and Saint-Martin use Guadeloupe’s grid, Wallis and Futuna New Caledonia’s, Saipan Guam’s; Kerguelen the world average. The carbon-intensity note names Ukraine (2022) among the older rows.
  • hurwitz_zeta() handles a non-positive non-integer q (8.93 at q = -0.5 for s = 2) and refuses a pole; top_share() refuses a fraction outside [0, 1] (0 is a share of nothing); hill_tail_index() refuses a vector x_min; rapl_available() refuses a non-path; exposure_concentration_index() refuses an infinite exposure. The masking-cost sentence of the side-channel vignette carries the measured 17 ms against 2.4 ms. crf_pm25() and crf_no2() refuse a logical exposure.
  • Third pass over the branch (4b4af29): top_share(x, 0) is zero units again and apply_schema_validation(data, NULL) means nothing to validate (two guards of the second pass overshot and turned CI red); capsule_verify() checks the shape of a signature before the type of the key, so an HMAC signature whose scheme was edited to XMSS is FALSE while a real XMSS signature with a string for a key is still an error; a FIPS signature whose recorded context or prehash is not a string is FALSE; verify_pollution() with a missing reference is a report, not a crash; briggs_plume_rise() at ambient temperature has zero flux and zero rise (a cooler stack is refused); Ctrl-C at the rmbl login --token prompt interrupts at once (the terminal line is read by a shell child, so the interrupt is not held until Enter); the yoy_pdf() notes test asserts the page rule instead of comparing a value with itself; the dead-stack note on the two gadget pairs says what they hold. Verifying an XMSS signature or attestation that still carries key_state warns that the key is compromised.

Review of the 0.5.12 branch

  • An XMSS attestation carried the signer’s private key. capsule_attest() embedded the whole signature object, and an XMSS signature carries key_state (the advanced key, with sk_seed and sk_prf) so the signer can save it. Anyone given such an attestation could attest anything under the victim’s public key. The key is stripped before the signature is embedded (as the recode manifest already did), and a test checks no attestation carries a secret. If you shared an XMSS attestation made by 0.5.11 or earlier, treat that key as compromised: generate a new one and re-attest. HMAC and ML-DSA attestations were never affected.
  • The composed TVLA kernels never ran: the harness wrote only the fifth argument to the stack, so the six-argument kernels faulted before a trace was taken, and the ML-DSA kernel’s conditional subtraction compiled to a branch, so its trace length varied. Fixed: every stack argument is written per the AAPCS, the subtraction is an arithmetic-shift mask, and the kernels’ glue handles one share per pass with the registers scrubbed between passes (the first measurement put 174 and 34 transition-model leaks in that glue, none in a gadget). The 0.5.12 note below says what the measurement now shows.
  • (Superseded by the second pass above, which keeps the line break.) The French SIU boilerplate fix overshot: a stripped sentence was replaced by a line break, so boilerplate in the middle of a roster line turned the rest of the line into a line of its own and counted 3 officers where every earlier version counted 1 (147 new divergences on a 6,017-input fuzz). The sentence is replaced by a space, the two 0.5.11 cases still count, and a property test inserts the boilerplate at every position of a line and checks the count never moves.
  • verify_pollution(exposure_mean = 0, exposure_prevalence = 1) and (25, 0) are valid runs with zero attributable cases again; “no data” is now only a call that passed neither. Every pipeline stage runs inside the status contract (a text income column, all-zero exposure, one row and a per-100,000 baseline_rate are reports, not raw errors); a factor argument is refused; the assumption log prints population=1,000,000.
  • The baseline-rate check went into pollution_burden() and pollution_burden_by_area() (800 per 100,000 taken per person-year gave 110 million deaths from a million people), and the message says which function takes the per-100,000 form. crf_no2() refuses a logical or factor beta_per_10 (TRUE gave a relative risk of e). n_bootstrap must be whole.
  • apply_schema_validation() refuses a list that mixes rules with anything else, a nested rule list and a data frame, instead of falling through to the provenance checker and passing.
  • advection_diffusion_2d() caps the work (cells x steps x sub-steps, 10 million, about five seconds) rather than the sub-step count: a 5 x 5 grid at 10,001 sub-steps runs in a tenth of a second and is allowed, a 201 x 201 grid at 9,999 for 100 steps would take hours and is refused. The cap no longer rounds 10,000 up to 10,001. A negative source and a logical u are refused; a receptor below ground or above the mixing lid is warned about; the open boundary is documented.
  • A configured Ollama server that does not answer is skipped with a message, like one with no model pulled, so a prompt that leaves for the hosted tier because a local route failed is always said. credentials.json (shared with morie and rmorie) that does not parse is an error and is never written over; llm.json that is not a JSON object ([], "x", 5) is an error too, not a warning that fired once and then let a saved route be dropped. The hosted key is tied to the address it was saved for; a new own.url or ollama.url drops the key saved for the old server; ollama.url refuses a metadata or link-local address when saved.
  • bricklayer_data_load() checks the manifest’s SHA-256 of a cached or downloaded table and deletes and refuses one that does not match.
  • fips_verify_mu() answers FALSE to a length-2 signature field (the shared hex helper takes one string); an XMSS signature whose index or height is not a whole number, or whose root, height, wire or randomizer was removed, is not verified, and a missing randomiser is FALSE rather than an error.
  • Time zones of territories the carbon table has no row for (Monaco, Vaduz, Andorra, the Channel Islands, the Antarctic stations: 41 zones) resolve to the grid of the country they draw on or to the world average, with the method saying so; they fell through to the locale, which made them the United States under en_US.
  • rmbl data list keeps accents in a C locale (control characters only are stripped); rmbl ask -- --like-this passes a prompt that starts with --; inst/bin/rmbl is executable in git; the help and the vignette suggest login --token with the key pasted at the prompt, never on the command line.
  • yoy_pdf() sizes its notes to the line allowance the pagination made, and many notes go on pages of their own (30 notes on a 5-inch page lost notes 24 to 30).
  • plot_lorenz() sorts a hand-made frame and refuses one that is not a Lorenz curve; an all-NA axis no longer breaks the margin computation. lagrangian_particles(n = 2.7) and compute_footprint(usage = c(...)) are refused.
  • Documentation: masking costs the measured 2.3 to 3.4 times on decapsulation and 7 to 10 times on signing (the help said 3 to 12 and 13 to 24). location = "GLOBAL" is an error since the duplicate row went (use "WORLD"); the rows older than 2024 include Ukraine (2022).

Cryptography

  • Masked ML-KEM decapsulation left the re-encryption shares on the dead stack: r0/r1, e10/e11, e20/e21, u0/u1, v0/v1, the FO-check shares ok/msk and the masked PRF’s input and output buffers (whose sum is the coins G(m' || h)[32..64]). Summing the two halves of r-hat recovers m' from the public key and ciphertext alone, so a memory disclosure anywhere in the process was a decryption oracle for an attacker-chosen ciphertext. Every pair the scanner can see is wiped now, with the per-group and per-word temporaries; two gadget-internal 32-coefficient pairs (sec_in_interval, sec_b2a) remain on the dead stack (they hold e2 + eta and v' - lo; v' contains Decompress(m’), so the second pair also encodes 32 bits of m’ for a chosen ciphertext: partial leakage, no key recovery shown), and one dsa_bprime pair remains on clang -O2. The 0.5.10 note that “every share pair is now wiped” was false and is corrected.
  • Masked ML-DSA signing wipes the bitsliced share temporaries of every 32-coefficient chunk (the low-bits test of v = w - c s2, the high bits of w and of the hint) as it goes; one chunk of v survived on some builds and revealed part of c t0.
  • Two composed TVLA kernels, next to the single gadgets: the ML-KEM decapsulation spine (s*u, w = v - su, Compress_1, a Keccak permutation over the message shares) and the ML-DSA z path (y from Boolean shares, z = y + c s1, the norm test, the low-bits test), so the hand-over between gadgets is measured too (the harness fix that let them run is above; the tvla workflow reports the value-model and transition-model t-statistics). The dudect gate on a DIT-capable CPU is the no-evidence line (|t| > 4.5 after the tripled re-measurement fails), not |t| > 10.
  • The ctcheck harness scans the dead stack for share pairs, not only for copies of a secret: any two windows whose coefficient-wise sum mod q (or XOR, for Boolean shares) is a known value count as a remnant. The ML-KEM case recomputes r-hat and m' from the message it encapsulated and scans for both after the masked decapsulation; this is the check that would have caught the gap above.
  • capsule_verify() answers FALSE, not an error, for a signature whose signature field is not one string, whose prehash names no digest, or whose XMSS auth, randomizer or index is missing; and an XMSS signature whose own root, height or wire disagrees with the key or with its parts no longer verifies (verification used the key’s values and ignored the edited fields).

Location, emissions

  • Time-zone aliases map to their own country. The table gave every backward alias the country of the zone it links to, which is wrong whenever the link crosses a border: Iceland was Ivory Coast (Africa/Abidjan), Atlantic/Jan_Mayen Germany, America/Coral_Harbour Panama, Africa/Asmera Kenya, Pacific/Truk Papua New Guinea. The builder now reads the #= annotation of the IANA backward file (the zone the alias stood for before the merge), takes the target’s country only when that target serves a single country in zone1970.tab, and keeps a reviewed table (tools/timezone_alias_countries.csv) for the remaining cross-border aliases; the generic zones CET, EET, MET, WET, EST, HST, MST and the *ST*DT names resolve to no country. Rebuilt from tzdata 2026e.
  • detect_location() warns when RMBL_LOCATION names a location the table does not know instead of silently moving on to the time zone.
  • compute_footprint() rejects a fractional cores.
  • The duplicate GLOBAL row (480 gCO2e/kWh from the Green Algorithms file) is gone from the carbon-intensity table; WORLD (Ember, 458.29) is the world average, and location = "GLOBAL" is now an error. The documentation no longer claims every row is from 2024 or 2025.

Air pollution and dispersion

  • verify_pollution() with no exposure data at all (no CSV, no demo, mean and prevalence both zero) is an "error" report with exit status 2, not a clean run with zero deaths; an exposure at or below the reference stays a valid run with zero attributable cases. The input contract is enforced in the report rather than as raw R errors: a vector where a single number is expected, a missing or negative reference, an unknown outcome, a non-logical demo, a directory as exposure_csv. The report prints the population as 1,000,000, not 1e+06. The vignette’s failure demo fails again.
  • advection_diffusion_2d() refuses a run that would need more than 10,000 sub-steps per step (dt = 1e5 on the previous round’s reproducer meant 7.8 million sub-steps, with the warning deferred until the end) and a wind that overflowed the sub-step count to NA; c0 must be a non-negative numeric matrix (a vector gave a field of mass 0) and source finite.
  • briggs_plume_rise() rejects temperatures below 150 K, which are Celsius values typed where kelvin is expected (111 m of rise instead of 51).
  • lagrangian_particles() rejects a grid whose bounds are reversed or whose cell counts are not whole (it gave a negative concentration).
  • crf_pm25() and crf_no2() take exactly one finite reference_conc (a vector recycled against the exposures; NA gave NA risks). attributable_fraction() rejects a logical relative risk. mortality_displaced() rejects a baseline rate above 1 (a per-100,000 figure passed where a per person-year rate is expected gave 23 million deaths from a million people).
  • plr_crossfit() requires a whole k_folds (2.7 ran with 2) and numeric columns (a factor outcome was analysed by its level codes).
  • exposure_concentration_index() refuses a factor or character income instead of ranking level codes, and negative exposures; pollution_burden_by_area() requires numeric exposure, population and baseline columns. The index’s n_quintiles field, a constant 5, is gone, and the documentation says ties share their average rank.
  • hurwitz_zeta() takes one q.
  • attributable_fraction(rr_lower =, rr_upper =) carries the relative risk’s confidence limits through Levin’s formula; crf_pm25() and crf_no2() carry the published 95 percent limits of their risks (rr_lower, rr_upper; NA for the IER forms), and verify_pollution() reports the fraction’s interval.

Language models

  • In the automatic order, a local Ollama server that answers with no model pulled, or a configured one that does not answer, is skipped with a message naming the route taken instead (“local Ollama at … has no model pulled; using the hosted MORIE tier”), so a prompt never leaves the machine silently.
  • A malformed llm.json is an error and no setting is written over it: the next config set used to rewrite the file with only the new value, deleting the saved keys and addresses.
  • A saved key belongs to the address it was saved with: MORIE_LLM_BASE_URL=... or OLLAMA_HOST=... set for one call receives the environment’s key or none, never the key saved for another server (the /api/tags probe included).
  • rmbl ask --model x --model y ... is a usage error instead of sending “–model y” in the prompt; --route auto takes the automatic order over a saved route; an invalid MORIE_LLM_ROUTE is an error, not silently “auto”.
  • config set own.url runs the same address check as use (a metadata or link-local address is refused when saved); ollama.url must be http(s).
  • A key typed at a terminal prompt is not echoed (where stty exists), and the help no longer suggests putting the key on the command line.
  • rmbl data list strips control characters from the manifest before printing.

Data validation, plots, reports

  • apply_schema_validation() accepts a rule list and runs it with validate_rules() under the same stop-on-fatal contract; it used to ignore a rule list in its second argument and report a pass, which is what the vignette told readers to do.
  • The French SIU resolver: a stripped boilerplate sentence is replaced by a space, so a roster entry after it on the same line (“… n’est pas divulgué. AI no 3 A participé”) is counted again; the 0.5.11 speed rewrite kept the sentence’s terminator and lost those entries (an unresolved report and a count of 1 instead of 3 on the two cases now pinned as tests).
  • Plot state is reset when a panel plot errors (the next plot’s title showed as “A”). plot_funnel() requires one area label per point. An empty frequency_table() draws an empty page with a title, and plume_field() requires increasing coordinates, with messages of their own instead of errors from inside the palette or base graphics.
  • yoy_pdf() paginates on the rows that fit the page height after the title block, the page label and the notes (.yoy_rows_per_page(), with a test); a 24-inch page planned 98 rows where 88 fit and dropped the last rows.
  • PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 is checked against the RFC 7914 vectors; the agent_bundle() help says which route the request takes.

Packaging

  • The rOpenSci pkgcheck workflow fails when pkgcheck does, and no longer asks for issues: write.
  • Text corrections: 118 registered entry points (not 113); the ACVP PBKDF set is SHA2-224 only and does not cover PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256; the plain path’s speed advantage is three to four times for decapsulation and seven to eleven for signing (not “about five”); a clean ctgrind run is evidence for that binary on the inputs run, not a proof for every input; the ChipWhisperer firmware is in the separate review archive, not in the package.

rmoriebricklayer 0.5.11

Language models: set everything from the shell or R

  • A stored hosted key is used even when a local Ollama server is running with no model pulled. The automatic route used to stop at that empty server (“local Ollama has no model to use”), so a user who had logged in, and whose doctor listed every hosted model, could not reach any of them. An empty Ollama is now passed over unless OLLAMA_MODEL is set or the Ollama route is asked for.
  • bricklayer_llm_config() and rmbl config show and save every language-model setting: the route ask takes (auto, own, ollama, hosted) and the address, key and model of your own server, of Ollama and of the hosted tier. rmbl config setup walks through them. Settings are saved in ~/.config/morie/llm.json (mode 0600); an environment variable that is set still wins.
  • rmbl ask --route ROUTE picks the route for one call.
  • rmbl doctor ends with the route and model ask will use, and how to change it.
  • rmbl help is a guide: the verbs by area, and help start, help llm, help config and help r pages with examples. Error messages name the config command that fixes them.

The table list reads left to right

  • rmbl data list and printing bricklayer_data_tables() in R show one line per table: the key, the row count and the name, left-aligned and cut to the terminal or console width. They went through print.data.frame, which right-aligned the names and, once the descriptions made a line wider than the terminal, printed every key, then every name, then every row count and source as separate blocks. bricklayer_data_tables() still returns the full data frame (with source); only its printing changed.
  • A table whose manifest entry has a blank description and source (the otis tables) is named by its key instead of by an empty string.
  • The smoke suite (inst/smoke/smoke.R) prints a failing case’s message in full. It cut them at 400 characters, which shortened “https://rmorie.com/access” in the no-route message of ask to “https://rmorie.co”.

rmoriebricklayer 0.5.10

A version of its own. The build tagged 0.5.9 on 2026-10-07 (29ff122) and the one that followed it the same day (dcb3cb9) shared a version number while differing in the masking defaults, the FIPS 203 section 7.3 key check, capsule_attest(context = raw) and the whole air-pollution feature. The stress test of dcb3cb9 (2026-10-08) asked for a number that tells them apart, and for the fixes below; this is both.

Every result draws itself

  • plot() methods for every result the package returns, on base graphics only: stock and flow (stock_flow(), one panel per measure), period-over-period change with intervals (yoy()), rates, shares and rate change, band sensitivity, drift by column (capsule_drift(), drift_calibrate()), Benford digits, power curves, frequencies, missingness patterns, region coverage, Mahalanobis outliers, correlations, permutation nulls, rounding envelopes, concentration-response curves, burdens, concentration curves, the whole verify_pollution() report on one page, the footprint with its equivalents, concentration fields and particle clouds, count trends, and analyse_table() one panel at a time. The same customisation everywhere (main, col or palette, grid, ... to the base call), bricklayer_plot_options() for the session, bricklayer_palette() with four colour-blind-safe palettes, and every method returns the data it drew. plume_field() evaluates a plume on a grid; plot_lorenz() and plot_funnel() serve the results that are plain data frames. vignette("plotting-results"). Titles fit their panel: a title too wide is drawn a step smaller, in a panel set one that still does not fit becomes a letter with the key printed under the panels (returned as the panel_key attribute), long axis titles shrink or wrap, and the left margin is sized from the widest tick label so an axis title never overlaps the numbers.
  • To carry what the plots need, exposure_concentration_index() records its concentration curve, count_trend() its data, verify_pollution() returns class rmbl_pollution_report, advection_diffusion_2d() class rmbl_field and lagrangian_particles() class rmbl_particles (all still plain lists underneath).

Air pollution and dispersion, after the stress test

  • verify_pollution() applied the PM2.5 counterfactual (5.8) to NO2, overstating NO2 deaths by 27%; reference now defaults per pollutant (NO2 10, PM2.5 5.8), as pollution_burden() always did.
  • Levin’s formula was diluted twice when prevalence was below 1: the relative risk was taken at the population mean, which already includes the unexposed, and then multiplied by the prevalence again. With a CSV or the demo data the exposed are the rows above the counterfactual floor: exposure_mean is their mean and exposure_prevalence their share, and the scalar arguments are documented the same way.
  • advection_diffusion_2d() documented a stability criterion that was false (cfl below 1 and diffusion number below 1); the explicit upwind-plus-FTCS scheme needs |u dt/dx| + |v dt/dy| + 2 (kx dt/dx^2 + ky dt/dy^2) <= 1, and a run outside it reached 10^10 from a unit pulse while reporting itself stable. The bound is returned as stability_number and stable; a call outside it is taken in enough sub-steps of a smaller dt to satisfy it (reported, with a warning), so the field is a solution over the same physical time rather than an explosion.
  • Physical guards throughout the dispersion code, on the package’s own input helpers: emission rates, masses, heights and distances non-negative, wind speed, travel time and grid steps positive, n_images a whole number (2.5 was truncated silently), the stack hotter than the air for Briggs’ rise (a cooler stack returned NaN), x0 and y0 single numbers (a vector doubled mean_x), and a warning when the release is above the mixing height. gaussian_plume(q = -100) returned a negative concentration and u = 0 returned Inf; gaussian_puff(t = -100) a negative one; pg_sigmas(-500) a negative sigma.
